file_id: M-S. Mourya Reddy Filling Station, vs The State Of Telangana, on 6 March, 2025

sentences.text:
M/S. Mourya Reddy Filling Station, vs The State Of Telangana,
on 6 March, 2025
 The Honourable Sri Justice J.Sreenivas Rao
 Writ Petition No.6873 of 2025
Order:

entities.text: Mourya Reddy Filling Station, vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This writ petition is filed seeking the following relief:
" ... to issue a Writ Order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondents in harassing the petitioners by issuing impugned Notice i e For Way Entry / Exit Notice dated 10.02.2025 issued by the 9th respondent threatening to remove the petrol bunk of the petitioner by name M/s.Mo urya Reddy Filling Station in Sy.No.723/2 situated at Rudraram Village Shivar, Patancheru Mandal, Sangareddy District as illegal, arbitrary, null and void and violation of Article 14 and 21 of the Constitution of India and consequently direct the respondents to withdraw the impugned Notice i.e., For Way Entry / Exit Notice dated 10.02.2025 issued by the 9th respondent by allowing the petitioner to run his business i e M/s Mourya Reddy Filling Station as usual."

2. Heard Sri J.Kanakaiah, learned Senior Counsel representing Sri J.Narendar, learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition for respondent Nos.1 and 4 to 6, Sri V.T.Kalyan, learned Standing Counsel for respondent Nos.2 and 3 and learned Government Pleader for Roads and Buildings for respondent Nos.7 to 9.
3.
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the writ petition is being disposed of at the stage of admission.

4. Facts giving rise to filing of this writ petition briefly stated are that the petitioner is the absolute owner and possessor of the land to an extent of Ac.0.37 gts and Ac.2.12 gts in Sy.Nos.768/5 and 723/2, situated at Rudraram Village, Patancheru Mandal, Sangareddy District.

The petitioner obtained license from M/s.Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited to run retail outlet and established at KM502/058-103 (RHS) on NH-65 of Pune to Hyderabad in Sy.No.723/2, situated at Rudraram Village, Patanchery Mandal, Sangareddy District (herein after referred to as "subject property") and conducting his business since 2022, without any objections.
The respondent authorities are trying to dispossess the petitioner from the subject property, under the guise of widening of road.

At that time, the petitioner along with others approached this Court and filed W.P.No.31694 of 2024 and this Court disposed of the said Writ Petition on 13.11.2024, directing the respondents therein to follow due process of law, in the event the lands of the petitioners are required for the purpose of expansion of existing 100 feet National Highway No.65.

The respondent No.9 without following any due process of law, as per the orders passed by this Court in W.P.No.31694 of 2024, straightaway issued impugned notice dated 10.02.2025 and aggrieved by the M/S. Mourya Reddy Filling Station, vs The State Of Telangana, on 6 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93745416/
1 same, the petitioner filed the present writ petition.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. Learned Senior Counsel submitted that the respondent authorities without following due procedure as contemplated under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act 30 of 2013),
straightaway issued impugned notice dated 10.02.2025 to the petitioner, directing him to remove the petrol bunk in the subject property and the same is gross violation of the provisions of the Act 30 of 2013 as well as 300-A of the Constitution of India.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act 30 of 2013)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 6. Learned Government Pleader for Roads and Buildings submitted that the subject property was occupied by the National Highway authority and respondent No.9 has rightly issued impugned notice dated 10.02.2025 and if the petitioner submits detailed explanation, pursuant to the impugned notice dated 10.02.2025, respondent No.9 will consider the same and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law.

7. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition and Sri V.T.Kalyan, learned Standing Counsel, reiterated the very same submissions made by the learned Government Pleader for Roads and Buildings.

8. By way of reply, learned Senior Counsel submitted that the petitioner may be granted liberty to submit detailed explanation to the impugned notice dated 10.02.2025, issued by respondent No.9.
9.

Having considered the rival submissions made by the respective parties and after perusal of the material available on record, it reveals that the petitioner is claiming right over the subject property and he is running petrol bunk, since 2022, pursuant to the permission granted by the competent authority.
Respondent No.9 issued impugned notice on 10.02.2025.

Thereafter, M/s.Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited submitted letter dated 17.02.2025 before respondent No.9.
10.

Taking into consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and submissions of respective parties, this Court deems it appropriate to dispose of the writ petition, granting liberty to the petitioner to submit detailed explanation to the impugned notice, dated 10.02.2025, issued by respondent No.9, within a period of one week from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and on such explanation, respondent No.9 is directed to consider the same and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, after giving notice and opportunity to the petitioner, including personal hearing, within a period of two (2) weeks from thereafter.
However, it is made clear that till such time, respondents are directed not to take any coercive steps in respect of the subject property.
11. With the above direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
No costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.
There shall be order as to costs.
J. SREENIVAS RAO, J Date: 06.03.2025
Note: Issue CC in three days b/o vsl M/S. Mourya Reddy Filling Station, vs The State Of Telangana, on 6 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93745416/
